How to find and claim a deceased person's unclaimed money in Australia

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 23 Nov 2026

Search ASIC's Moneysmart unclaimed money register for old bank accounts, shares and life insurance, and your state's register for other money (in Queensland, the Public Trustee; in NSW, Revenue NSW). There's no time limit on claiming money held by ASIC. Only the executor or administrator can claim for the estate. For ASIC-held shares money they use Claim form B with probate, or with a certified death certificate and will if the amount is $20,000 or less. Bank-account money is claimed through the bank's unclaimed money team.

Key facts

  • Only the executor or administrator can claim for an estate
  • ASIC: no time limit; about 60 days to process
  • ASIC shares money: will + death certificate if $20,000 or less
  • Bank-account money: claim through the bank

What are the steps?

  1. Search ASIC's register on Moneysmart by name (or Original Transaction Number). It covers money from lost bank accounts, shares and investments, and life insurance. Service NSW notes bank accounts become unclaimed after 7 years with no deposits or withdrawals.
  2. Search the state register too. Queensland Public Trustee holds money from Queensland government agencies, businesses such as solicitors, real estate agents and nursing homes, unclaimed wages and deceased estate entitlements. It doesn't hold old bank accounts, life insurance, super or rental bonds. In NSW, search Revenue NSW's register.
  3. Note the reference: the OTN for ASIC records, or the reference number for Queensland Public Trustee.
  4. Shares and investments ('Company money') held by ASIC: the executor or administrator completes Claim form B - Representative, with all executors claiming. Provide certified ID for each, proof of the deceased's address or connection to the company, and a certified copy of probate including the full will. With a will but no probate, certified copies of the death certificate and will are enough unless the funds exceed $20,000.
  5. Old bank accounts: contact the bank that held the account and ask for its unclaimed money team. ASIC only assesses these claims when they come through the bank.
  6. Queensland Public Trustee: all executors sign the application, a Justice of the Peace witnesses it, and you post it with certified ID, linking documents, the will, the death certificate and the grant of probate or letters of administration (or a statutory declaration from all executors if there isn't one). Money is paid to an estate bank account, or by cheque to the estate.
  7. Revenue NSW: select 'Deceased estate' in its online claim. The executor or administrator provides ID, the grant (or will and death certificate) and a document linking the deceased to the address on record; all executors must be part of the claim.
  8. No will? ASIC asks you to email it first with the beneficiaries, the estate's value, place and date of death, usual residence and confirmation that no grant was made. Revenue NSW says you need formal administration and suggests contacting NSW Trustee and Guardian.
  9. Lost super is separate: once the ATO records you as the legal personal representative, its deceased estate data package includes details of any super accounts.

Frequently asked questions

How do I find unclaimed money for a deceased person in Australia?

Search ASIC's unclaimed money register on Moneysmart (bank accounts, shares and investments, life insurance) and the state register, such as Queensland Public Trustee or Revenue NSW. Anyone can search a name, but only the executor or administrator can claim for the estate.

Who can claim unclaimed money for a deceased estate?

The executor or administrator. ASIC requires all executors to claim on Claim form B, Queensland Public Trustee says the executor is the only person eligible, and Revenue NSW requires all executors or administrators to be part of the claim.

Do I need probate to claim unclaimed money from ASIC?

Not for smaller amounts. For shares and investments money, ASIC accepts certified copies of the death certificate and will if the funds are $20,000 or less. Over $20,000, probate must be provided.

Is there a time limit to claim unclaimed money?

Not for money lodged with ASIC. Service NSW notes it can be claimed at any time by the rightful owner, and interest is paid from 1 July 2013.

How long does an unclaimed money claim take?

ASIC says about 60 days once it has the correct documents. Queensland Public Trustee aims for up to 28 days from receiving all documents, and Revenue NSW asks you to allow up to 28 days.

How do I claim a dead person's old bank account money?

Contact the bank that originally held the account and ask for its unclaimed money team. The bank verifies the claim and submits it to ASIC, and the funds come back through the bank.
